note: Documents, media and the Bunny components that are themselves capsuled. Bunny's own surfaces appear here so that they are subject to the same declaration ceiling as everything else; a system component with no catalogue entry would be an application the trust layer could not refuse anything to.

entries.name: LibreOffice
entries.purpose: Write documents, build spreadsheets and make presentations.

permissionReasons.files: to open the document you choose and save your changes
permissionReasons.folders: to keep a document and the files it links to together
permissionReasons.notifications: to tell you when a long export has finished
permissionReasons.network: to fetch the extension list when you ask for one

entries.differences: Reads and writes Microsoft's formats well but not perfectly: complex Word layouts, tracked changes in long documents and Excel macros are where it differs. It has no cloud co-authoring. Everything stays on this computer.

entries.name: Microsoft 365
entries.purpose: The commercial office suite, in a browser on this computer.
entries.sandboxNote: There is no Linux desktop build. The web version runs in your browser, so its isolation is the browser's, and your documents live on Microsoft's servers rather than on this computer.
entries.differences: Perfect fidelity with its own formats, real co-authoring, and a subscription with an account. Your documents are stored on Microsoft's servers by default, which is the difference that matters if they are confidential.

entries.name: Document Viewer

permissionReasons.files: to open the document you chose
permissionReasons.notifications: to tell you when printing has finished

entries.differences: Reads documents; it does not edit them. Comes with Bunny OS and needs nothing installed.

entries.name: Files
entries.purpose: Browse and organise your own files.

permissionReasons.folders: to show you your own folders, which is what a file manager is
permissionReasons.notifications: to tell you when a copy has finished
permissionReasons.usb: to show you a drive you plug in

entries.sandboxNote: A file manager whose job is to see your files cannot be given a sandbox that hides them. It runs with resource limits and an audit trail instead, and Bunny says so rather than drawing a boundary that is not there.
entries.differences: Part of Bunny OS. Nothing to install.

entries.name: Text Editor
entries.purpose: Write and edit plain text and notes.

permissionReasons.files: to open and save the file you are editing

entries.differences: Plain text only — no formatting, no page layout. Part of Bunny OS, so there is nothing to install and nothing to update separately.
